The fix (whether an original patch or a revision to an existing one) must address a root cause and stay within these guardrails (the `flaky-test-investigator` skill's pitfalls carry the full rationale):

- Do not weaken assertions, wrap assertions **or interactions** in `retry()` / `retry.tryForTime` (re-issuing a click/type/navigation so a "missed" interaction registers on a later attempt hides a real actionability bug, not just wrapping an `expect`), bump timeouts as the primary fix, or strip tags to skip the test.
- Wait on readiness signals instead of retrying outcomes. When the state the test must wait on has no DOM footprint (e.g. an async parse in a worker), prefer a small application-side change that exposes one (a `data-test-subj` or attribute) over re-issuing actions until the outcome looks right: re-running actions also re-fires their side effects.
- Never patch shared test-framework infrastructure with retries or error tolerance. Adding a retry, poll, or error-swallowing loop to a framework package or shared service (`kbn-test*`, `kbn-ftr-*`, the Scout framework packages such as `@kbn/scout` and its derivatives) — including "retry on transient network error" around an HTTP or auth call — is the same cheap masking as a test-side retry, amplified to every suite that shares the code. Diagnose why the operation fails and fix that; when the root cause lives in infrastructure you can't fix here, hand the diagnosis to the owning team instead. Updating a page object or a suite's fixtures to wait on a concrete readiness signal remains a legitimate fix — this rules out tolerance patches to shared framework code, not page-object/fixture improvements.
- Use the framework's documented public API only. Never widen a framework package's public surface to enable a fix — e.g. exporting an internal tag-computation helper instead of using the documented `tags` constants. If the documented API can't express the fix, that's a feature request for the framework's owning team, not something a fix PR should smuggle in.
- Follow the testing best practices in `docs/extend/testing/` (`scout-best-practices.md`, `ui-best-practices.md`, `api-best-practices.md`), even where the surrounding test file predates them: an existing retry-wrapped interaction nearby is legacy to fix, not a pattern to copy.
